comments.body:
Pushed as Gerrit 1941 (Change-Id Ibb5fb5425d4635019302a4956a5cdc7071d7b84f).

WHAT LANDED
- scripts/amend_commit_message.py — reads HEAD's Change-Id (`git log -1
  --format=%B`), strips any Change-Id line from FILE (Gerrit rejects two), puts
  HEAD's back via `git interpret-trailers` (so placement next to Signed-off-by is
  git's job, not a reimplementation), then `git commit --amend --file <tmp>`.
  No --no-verify: the pre-commit + commit-msg gates still fire.
- Makefile `amend-msg` target (+ .PHONY), usage error exit 2 when FILE is unset.
- AGENTS.md "Push for review" bullet now names `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` for a
  REWRITTEN message and states that `--amend -m/-F` drop the Change-Id and open a
  duplicate change.
- tests/unit/test_amend_msg_change_id.py — 7 tests.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL (AC 2), and why it is not decorative
Both halves run in ONE throwaway repo from ONE starting commit:
  1. seed commit is stamped by a fake Gerrit hook -> Change-Id I...0001;
  2. NAIVE `git commit --amend -F msg` -> asserts the id CHANGED (I...0002). If it
     had not, the test fails with "negative control is inert" — the fixture itself
     is proven able to distinguish a working wrapper from a no-op one;
  3. `git reset --hard <seed>` back to the identical commit;
  4. the wrapper -> asserts the id is still I...0001 AND that the message was
     really rewritten (new subject present, seed subject absent, sha changed).
The fake hook's counter lives in .git/, OUTSIDE the work tree, so `reset --hard`
does not rewind it: a wrapper that let the hook re-stamp yields a THIRD id
(I...0003), not a coincidental match with the first.

MUTATION-PROVED, not assumed. Sabotaging the wrapper two ways:
  A) make it a no-op (return 0, never amend)  -> 1 failed (the "message was really
     rewritten" assertion) — the vacuous-pass hole the AC warns about is closed.
  B) amend but drop the Change-Id (naive behaviour) -> 2 failed, with
     I...0003 != I...0001 exactly as the counter design predicts.
Restored -> 7 passed.

LOUD FAILURE (AC 3)
No Change-Id on HEAD -> exit non-zero, stderr names Change-Id and `make hooks`,
and the test asserts HEAD's sha is UNCHANGED — refusing, not amending-then-warning.
A missing/typo'd FILE is also non-zero with HEAD untouched (no amend to an empty
message).

OUT OF SCOPE, HONOURED (AC 5): no pre-push hook, no reflog comparison, no other
guard. Only the wrapper + the doc line.

DOGFOOD (extra signal, not the evidence)
Ran `make amend-msg` against this change's own commit through the REAL pre-commit
+ Gerrit commit-msg chain — something the tmp fixture cannot cover. Change-Id
Ibb5fb542... identical before and after, sha changed 1108a3f4 -> c7efbc91,
interpret-trailers placed it after Signed-off-by.

GATES
- make lint            exit 0
- make typecheck       exit 0 (mypy, 577 files)
- python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check (run DIRECTLY, not via lint):
  active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0
- python scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py  exit 0. The helper does fire this gate
  (it is a raw `git commit`), sanctioned with two `# raw-git-ok:` markers carrying
  reasons: the amend targets the CODE checkout's HEAD, never the ticket store,
  whose writes stay on the rebar seams. Markers had to sit on the line
  IMMEDIATELY above `def` — a multi-line comment block above that is not read.

DESIGN NOTE
Advisory E2 from the plan review (FILE carrying its own Change-Id -> two trailers,
which Gerrit rejects) is implemented and tested rather than left open. Advisory E4
(the description's parenthetical mis-attributes this repo's main-branch rail to
prepare-commit-msg; it is actually the pre-commit `no-commit-to-branch` hook, which
--no-verify DOES bypass) is recorded here rather than edited into the description,
since the hook-cannot-fix-it conclusion rests on the measured `-F` amend behaviour,
not on that parenthetical.

comments.body: Landed: Gerrit 1941 merged as 13c7fe9ae1 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, 0 unresolved. Orchestrator verified the landed change against origin/main independently: exactly four files (AGENTS.md +7, Makefile +19, scripts/amend_commit_message.py +185, tests/unit/test_amend_msg_change_id.py +261) and NO pre-push hook, reflog comparison, or other guard — the out-of-scope boundary held. AGENTS.md line 282 now names make amend-msg as the path for a rewritten message, cites the three duplicate changes this footgun produced today (1921, 1926, 1931), and documents the loud refusal when HEAD carries no Change-Id. The server-side rebase preserved Change-Id Ibb5fb5425d4635019302a4956a5cdc7071d7b84f — the same id the wrapper carried through its own dogfood amend, so the tool was validated end-to-end through a real Gerrit round-trip in addition to its fixture tests. Closing: the local full-suite run the implementing agent was waiting on is not the authoritative signal here — CI's Verified +1 ran the whole tree on the exact merged commit, and the local run was executing under concurrent interference from other sessions.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem
`git commit --amend -F <file>` (and `-m`) REPLACES the entire commit message, dropping the
`Change-Id` trailer. Gerrit's `commit-msg` hook then stamps a NEW Change-Id, so the next push
creates a SECOND Gerrit change instead of a new patchset on the existing one. The original change
is left orphaned and must be abandoned by hand.

This happened TWICE in one session (2026-08-19), producing abandoned duplicates Gerrit 1921 and
1926. Both agents recovered — restored the original Change-Id, re-pushed as a new patchset, and
abandoned the duplicate — so the cost is cleanup and reviewer confusion rather than lost work.

## A hook CANNOT fix this — measured, not assumed
`prepare-commit-msg` looked like the natural home (this repo already uses it as a clone-local rail
that blocks commits on `main`, and `--no-verify` does not bypass it). It does not work. Measured
directly in a throwaway repo:

| invocation | hook receives |
|---|---|
| `git commit --amend --no-edit` | `source='commit'  sha='HEAD'` — detectable |
| `git commit --amend -F <file>` | `source='message' sha=''` — **identical to a fresh `-F` commit** |

Git does not tell the hook that an `-F` amend is an amend, so the hook cannot distinguish "amending,
preserve the Change-Id" from "new commit, stamp one". Gerrit's own `commit-msg` hook is no help
either: by design it only ADDS a Change-Id when absent and does nothing when one is present.

Nor does the server catch it. Gerrit rejects the same Change-Id in multiple changes and multiple
Change-Id lines, but a commit carrying a FRESH Change-Id is indistinguishable from a legitimate new
change — which is exactly why both incidents produced silent duplicates rather than a push rejection.

## How the Gerrit ecosystem actually solves it (prior art)
Every large Gerrit project removes the failure mode by ensuring contributors never hand-run
`git commit --amend` + `git push refs/for/*`:

| project | wrapper |
|---|---|
| Go | `git codereview change` — creates a new commit, or amends the existing one PRESERVING the Change-Id |
| OpenStack / OpenDev | `git-review` (`git review`) |
| Android | `repo upload` |
| Chromium | `git cl upload` (depot_tools) |

The documented backstop is a prohibition: OpenStack's contributor guide states plainly not to use
`-m` to supply a commit message, because it overrides the previous message and regenerates the
Change-Id. `-F` behaves identically.

**No major Gerrit project implements a hook or pre-push guard for this.** They make the failure
UNREACHABLE rather than DETECTABLE.

## Scope
Follow the prior art. Add a thin wrapper and make it the documented path.

1. A `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` target (thin script if the Makefile recipe gets unwieldy) that
   amends HEAD with the contents of FILE while CARRYING FORWARD the existing `Change-Id` trailer
   from the current HEAD message. If HEAD has no Change-Id, it must fail loudly rather than
   silently amending — a missing trailer means the commit-msg hook is not installed, which is its
   own problem (`make hooks`).
2. Update `AGENTS.md` line ~280, which currently reads
   "Iterate on findings with `git commit --amend --no-edit` (keep the `Change-Id`) + re-push",
   to also name `make amend-msg FILE=…` as the path for a REWRITTEN message, and to state
   explicitly that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate change.

**EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE — do not build:** a `pre-push` hook, a reflog-based Change-Id comparison,
or any other novel guard. A reflog rail was designed and REJECTED for this ticket: no project in the
ecosystem does it, so we would be maintaining a bespoke hook with no prior art to borrow from when
it misfires, to detect a failure the wrapper prevents outright.

## Why this matters more here than upstream
Those projects' contributors are humans using `$EDITOR`, where the pull toward `-m`/`-F` is weak.
rebar's contributors are largely AGENTS composing raw git commands, for whom `-F` is the natural way
to write a multi-line message without shell-quoting pain. The remedy transfers; the incentive to
bypass it is stronger, which is why the wrapper must be the DOCUMENTED DEFAULT rather than merely
available.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `make amend-msg FILE=<path>` amends HEAD with FILE's contents and the resulting commit
      carries the SAME `Change-Id` as before the amend — proven by a test that captures the
      Change-Id before and after and asserts equality.
- [x] The same test proves the naive form still loses it: `git commit --amend -F <file>` on the
      same fixture yields a DIFFERENT (or absent) Change-Id. Without this contrast the first
      criterion can pass vacuously.
- [x] `make amend-msg` fails loudly and non-zero when HEAD carries no `Change-Id`, rather than
      producing a commit that will be stamped with a fresh one.
- [x] `AGENTS.md` names `make amend-msg` as the path for a rewritten commit message and states
      that `--amend -m` / `--amend -F` drop the Change-Id and create a duplicate Gerrit change.
- [x] No `pre-push` hook, reflog comparison, or other guard is added.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Provenance
Filed 2026-08-19 after two duplicate changes (Gerrit 1921, 1926) in one session. The hook-based
approach was investigated and empirically disproved before filing; the wrapper approach follows
Go, OpenStack, Android and Chromium practice.

file_impact.reason: Add the amend-msg target that carries the existing Change-Id trailer forward.
Name make amend-msg as the documented path for a rewritten commit message and warn that --amend -m/-F drop the Change-Id.

The wrapper itself: the plan allows a thin script when the Makefile recipe gets unwieldy, and reading HEAD Change-Id + stripping a stray one from FILE + interpret-trailers placement is past what a make recipe should carry.
Proves AC1 and AC2 together: the wrapper preserves the Change-Id AND, on the same fixture rewound to the same commit, naive git commit --amend -F loses it.

compiled_state.title: Add make amend-msg wrapper so amending a commit cannot drop its Change-Id
